acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce or bound the failure (for example -count=50 under parallel CPU load with the store package running) and record the outcome.
If confirmed: the implementer step's survivor or quiescence observation is made deterministic for this fixture, or the test waits on the condition it needs, and a repeated run under load passes.
If not reproducible: close with the evidence and attribute the failure elsewhere.
body:
Suspected flaky test (not yet confirmed as a defect). Observed 2026-10-05 on a loaded macOS host in a scratch clone of claude/502-typed-event-stage (base b1e37605, Go 1.27.1), during `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/tasks/store` (984s package run):

    --- FAIL: TestCALV0078_SupervisedRunAfterCommitIsNotRetryable/refresh-STOPPED (5.53s)
        program_gate_retry_test.go:149: implement: ... Phase:BLOCKED_RECOVERY ... Quiescence:SURVIVORS ... native transition refused: ... Outcome:VALIDATION_FAILED ... Detail:MALFORMED: transaction: program transition

The failure is in the setup step `w.RunRole(ctx, "implementer", "")`, before the injected fault point, so the case under test never ran. The subtest passed with -count=3 in isolation and in a full rerun of the same package set (844s).

Hypothesis: under host load the supervised implementer run observes surviving processes at quiescence, enters BLOCKED_RECOVERY, and the following program transition is refused, so the fixture never reaches BUILT. That would be a timing dependency in the fixture's quiescence observation, not a CAL-V0-078 defect.

Expected: the implementer step deterministically reaches BUILT, or the test reports a skip-with-reason when the host cannot prove quiescence. It should never fail on timing.

Actual: an intermittent FAIL before the fault point on a loaded host.
title: Suspected flake: TestCALV0078_SupervisedRunAfterCommitIsNotRetryable implementer step can end BLOCKED_RECOVERY under load
